what_changed:
I checked every reviewer finding against the files, the V2 transcripts and a Node probe. All of them hold. I found no honest scenario-only design, so the branch is reset to main (HEAD f7fdefd9), nothing is committed, and the scenario stays at Version 2 (Preflight skip, non-regression).

Reviewer findings:
1. BLOCKER, the fixture leaks the answer. Confirmed. Setup does `cp -R .../references maintaining-obsidian/references`. Lines 95-110 of references/audit.md restate the line under test ("The deterministic scans run in code... The four threshold flags take the vault's numbers from its SCHEMA.md `## Audit Thresholds`"), and the V3 fixture uses that exact heading.
2. BLOCKER, both arms list the tree. Confirmed. Lines 384-390 of scripts/lib/eval-trial.js add "every file you need is already in it" to every contained trial. All three V2 baseline trials (run 20260930-105529) made `find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | sort && ls -la .claude` their first call and `cat maintaining-obsidian/references/audit.md` their second. `lint_vault.py --help` describes its four flags one for one with the SCHEMA prose thresholds.
3. BLOCKER, no scenario-only fix exists. Confirmed after testing alternatives (below). Lines 236-239 of scripts/lib/eval.js show the treatment differs from the baseline only by SKILL.md prepended to the Context. So any file the treatment can reach sits in the trial tree the baseline lists.
4. Should-fix, the treatment's own instruction works against it. Confirmed. Lines 96-98 of audit.md say to resolve references/ against the announced base directory, "never against the user's working directory". No trial announces one.
5. Should-fix, the positive regex passes things it should not. Confirmed with a Node probe: a heredoc line quoting `python3 .../lint_vault.py` with all four flags returns true, an `echo "python3 lint_vault.py ..."` returns true, and `--field-empty-pct 85.5 --tag-min 5.5` returns true.
6. Note, the regex fails valid runs. Confirmed: `python3 -B`, `python3.12` and `uv run` all return false.
7. Note, `__pycache__` gets copied. Confirmed: the main checkout has vault_frontmatter/vault_links cpython-314.pyc in references/__pycache__/ (ignored by .gitignore:41), and `cp -R` carries them into the trial.

Findings 5-7 are moot because the V3 commit is discarded.

Alternatives I tested and rejected:
(a) Measure a SKILL.md line that audit.md does not restate, the "Close every operation" `audit | <scope>` log line. Rejected for two reasons. It is a different claim from this scenario's name. It would also sit at ceiling: the fixture's log.md already has an `## [2026-04-02] audit | 50 most recent` line, and all three V2 baselines appended an audit log line "following the vault's existing log format" (trial-1:70, trial-2:98, trial-3:78).
(b) Measure "Operating on: <name>". Rejected: it is a trivial echo and not this claim.
(c) Copy only the .py files and leave out audit.md. Rejected: the script stays visible in `find .`, and --help hands over the flag mapping. The treatment also loses the "audit.md says how to run it" file that SKILL.md points to.
(d) Leave the script out and assert that the agent searches for `lint_vault`. Rejected: it measures recall of a token from the injected text, in a situation that never happens in real use. That is a manufactured trap.
(e) Hide or rename the copy. Rejected: it tests file-finding, not the instruction.
baseline_expectation: With any scenario-only design, the baseline reaches the script and passes. The fixture has to put maintaining-obsidian/references/ in the trial directory, or the treatment cannot run the script. In run 20260930-105529, all three baseline trials listed the whole tree on call 1 and read audit.md on call 2. audit.md states the full behavior: run lint_vault.py with the four flags taken from SCHEMA.md's `## Audit Thresholds`. Even with only the script present, --help matches each flag to a SCHEMA threshold. The reviewer's re-grade of the three V2 baseline transcripts under the V3 assertions, with the values swapped, scored 1/1/1. So I expect V3 to BLOCK at 2 or 3 of 3, which would spend 3 preflight sessions to confirm what the files already show.
offline_evidence:
- Node probe of the V3 positive regex: the heredoc quote, the echo quote and the 85.5/5.5 values all return true; `python3 -B`, `python3.12` and `uv run` all return false.
- Transcript greps of 20260930-105529 trial-1/2/3: call 1 is `find .` in all three, call 2 reads audit.md, and each trial appends an audit log line.
- Code read: scripts/lib/eval.js:236-239 (the treatment only gets SKILL.md prepended to the Context); scripts/lib/eval-trial.js:384-390 (the isolation advisory); no "Base directory" string anywhere in scripts/.
- Skill read: audit.md:95-110 restates the SKILL.md lines on the script and the thresholds; audit.md:96-98 has the base-directory dependency.
- After `git reset --keep main` (HEAD f7fdefd9): the scenario is back at Version 2, `## Preflight skip`, `## Verdict Policy non-regression`, and `node scripts/cli.js eval lint eval-maintaining-obsidian-audit-runs-lint-script` reports ok.
- I used `--keep` rather than `--hard` so the dirty package-lock.json from npm install stays uncommitted and untouched, as the rules ask. The resulting branch state is identical to `--hard`.
- `npm test`, `npm run lint` and the static checks were not re-run, because the tree now matches main apart from package-lock.json.
- No live sessions were run.
backlog_wish: eval: in skill-scope A/B, give the treatment arm only a host-style `Base directory for this skill: <dir>` line, with that skill's files staged outside the trial tree the baseline can list (and allowed by the isolation advisory and guard for the treatment only), so lines that point at shipped scripts or references can be measured without putting them in the baseline's fixture.
finding_for_decision_log: eval-maintaining-obsidian-audit-runs-lint-script cannot discriminate as a skill-scope scenario. The treatment can reach lint_vault.py only if Setup copies references/ into the trial directory, where the baseline's first-call `find .` lists it next to audit.md, and audit.md restates the instruction under test (V2 preflight 20260930-105529 BLOCKed at 3/3 by exactly this route). The scenario stays at Version 2 as a treatment-only non-regression guard with its preflight skipped, until the engine can give only the treatment a base directory outside the trial tree.
unverified: No live behavior was measured. That V3 would BLOCK at 2-3 of 3 is a prediction from the V2 transcripts and the reviewer's re-grade, not a run. The engine wish (treatment-only base directory outside the listed tree) has not been prototyped. I have not checked whether the isolation guard can allow one path for one arm only.
